newsitem.title: USA: PrimeStar says News Corp deal not a merger.
newsitem.headline: PrimeStar says News Corp deal not a merger.

text.p: PrimeStar Partners on Wednesday said the satellite television company's deal with Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and MCI Communications Corp was not a proposal to merge News Corp.
"News Corp's role will be a very passive one from this point forward," Jim Gray, PrimeStar Partners chairman and chief executive, said at a press conference.

Gray and other PrimeStar executives spoke to reporters after the announcement early Wednesday that PrimeStar was planning to restructure from a partnership to a public company that will include U.S. satellite assets from News Corp and MCI.

PrimeStar said the preferred securities being paid to News Corp for two satellites and a high-power orbital position may be converted to no more than 20 percent of its outstanding non-voting common shares.
"News Corp will not have a strong influence on either the management and operations or the directional strategies of PrimeStar," Gray said.
News Corp will receive no preferential treatment for the inclusion of its local programming channels on the PrimeStar system, Gray said.
PrimeStar already carries New Corp's Family Channel and expects to add the Fox News and FX channels.

Gray said PrimeStar was indemnified against any liability stemming from litigation between News Corp and EchoStar Communications Corp after the collapse of the proposed alliance between those two companies.
PrimeStar hopes to close its conversion into a public company, to be called PrimeStar Inc, during the fourth quarter, Gray said.
The company aims to launch high-power direct-broadcast satellite services by the end of the first quarter in 1998.

The acquisition of high-power capability is expected to give a big boost to PrimeStar's market share in urban and suburban areas. PrimeStar currently offers only mid-power services, with most of its customers residing in rural areas.

PrimeStar presently controls about 30 percent of the direct broadcast satellite market, it said. With the addition of high-power capabilities, which allow customers to use smaller receiving dishes, the company sees expanding its market share beyond 40 percent.
PrimeStar said it expected to expand its capacity to about 240 channels with the introduction of new services, from a current capacity of 160.
